headline: Samsung's 12-layer HBM4E memory has reportedly passed quality tests by Nvidia and major cloud customers.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 6: the tests were passed at the end of September and the report dates from 7 Oct, and it is a single-source report with no supply deal.
importance_line: Passing qualification is the step before orders, so it improves Samsung's chances of supplying memory for AI processors, but no volumes, prices or shipment dates are reported.
summary: Hankyung reported on 7 Oct 2026, as relayed by Yahoo Finance and Digitimes, that Samsung Electronics' 12-layer HBM4E, a stacked high-bandwidth memory chip used with AI processors, passed qualification tests by Nvidia and major data-centre operators at the end of September. Passing the tests does not mean a supply contract has been signed.
notes: Digitimes page shows only the lead ('reportedly cleared customer quality validation'); full text read in the Yahoo Finance rewrite, which credits Hankyung.com (Korea Economic Daily). Event (test pass) was end of September, report 7 Oct, so older than the 8 Oct window.
